recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Revisit only if the work group wants additional profiling.html narrative about authoring practices for sliceIsConstraining; the normative datatype definition and invariant already implement the decision.
issue_request: FHIR-13545 was Published with resolution Persuasive with Modification for STU3 and requested a boolean marker so derived profiles can explicitly indicate whether a named slice constrains an inherited same-name slice.
initial_application: The Jira comment cites svn revision 14334; git commit becab2754dd6f6f16643d6a6c256c08bd8795c1a applied the issue by adding ElementDefinition.sliceIsConstraining to source/datatypes/elementdefinition.xml with the requested definition, requirements, comments, and invariant eld-22 requiring sliceName when the flag is present.
additional_context: The original resolution described ElementDefinition.slicing.constraining, but the contemporaneous conformance Zulip thread explains that slices do not carry ElementDefinition.slicing and that placing the marker there would break snapshot logic. The current top-level ElementDefinition.sliceIsConstraining placement is therefore an intentional refinement, not an omission. Related slicing-language issues FHIR-16309 and FHIR-17821 are already represented on the combined branch.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Current build-scope source lists ElementDefinition as an active datatype and defines ElementDefinition.sliceIsConstraining as a 0..1 boolean with the FHIR-13545 semantics plus the sliceName invariant.
